title: Factory and site acceptance testing (FAT/SAT) | Aquemi
meta: Wet factory acceptance testing in our test bay and site acceptance testing after installation, to written protocols you approve, following GAMP 5.
headline: Your system runs in our test bay before it ships
lead: Every skid passes a wet factory acceptance test (FAT) against a protocol you approve. After installation, a site acceptance test (SAT) confirms nothing changed in transport or tie-in. Results are written so your qualification team can rely on them.

blocks.h: Find problems where they are cheap to fix
body: A fault found in our shop costs a day. The same fault found on your site can cost a shutdown window. We run the system wet, with water flowing through every line, so leaks, sequence errors and instrument faults show up before shipment.
GAMP 5 allows qualification to use well-documented supplier testing. We write the FAT so that your IQ and OQ can reference it rather than repeat it, when your quality unit agrees.

blocks.h: A note on water quality at FAT
blocks.body: Our test bay runs on our own feedwater. Conductivity and total organic carbon (TOC) at FAT prove the system can perform. Compliance with USP <645> and USP <643> on your site is confirmed during SAT and qualification, on your feedwater.

items.q: Can we witness the FAT remotely?
items.a: Yes. We run a video link with a second camera on the HMI. Signatures can be collected electronically.

items.q: Do you test with our software version?
items.a: Yes. The PLC and HMI software tested at FAT is the version that ships, under version control.

items.q: How long does a FAT take?
items.a: Typically [days] for a packaged Purified Water skid, longer for a full generation and distribution system.

cta.body: Ask for our standard FAT protocol structure and adapt it to your URS.
